fixed_constraints: I50 reconciles documentation with shipped behavior: READMEs, the docs index, task ledger, coverage, plan, CLI guides, and new release notes must match actual command output, with proof, compatibility, obsolete-syntax, and unsupported-platform claims removed.
Historical design material stays labelled and linked, never silently rewritten as current authority; the v0.1 freeze rule itself forbids silent rewrites of the frozen contract.
No release notes file exists yet; signing, notarization, and upload stay open gates with prepared commands only, and no live provider quality is claimed.
Completion requires verified contract-to-evidence links, exact pins and limits, a clean-machine install-to-run pass, and a recount of all fifty checkboxes.
common.purpose: Settle three I50 documentation design points for Can: the fate of REQUIREMENTS.md, the release-notes shape, and the docs index scope.

index_scope.background: The docs index mixes dated design links with a status map and reading steps that assert live sketches, beside-sketch goldens, and a CAN-code registry that no longer exist.
facts: The index already labels its lower half historical and incomplete, yet its reading order still sends reviewers to deleted sketch programs and golden gates.
The authoritative current records are the task ledger, the coverage mapping, the evidence directories, and the package READMEs, none of which the index centers.
A minimal relabel keeps every existing anchor while a rebuild risks breaking deep links from evidence and review notes that cite current headings.

release_notes_shape.background: The candidate needs release notes recording shipped state, pins, open gates, install flow, and limits, either as a new implementation document or inside the distribution guide.
facts: distribution/README.md already documents install, upgrade, prepared signing commands, and the unsigned-release open gate across its I01/I02/I39 sections.
The root README, task ledger, and evidence READMEs all link outward for release truth, but no single notes file gathers version, pins, gates, and limits.
Implementation documents hold task evidence while distribution documents hold shipping procedure, so the notes sit at the boundary between the two audiences.

requirements_fate.background: The 288-line root REQUIREMENTS.md freezes a v0.1 contract of decision tables, given/call evidence, revision pins, and CAN codes that the shipped compiler retired.
facts: Its own freeze rule states rules are never rewritten silently and amendments land tagged, which a quiet in-place modernization would violate.
The docs index and root README cite it as the living contract and map readers to deleted sketch programs through it.
No current test, gate, or example enforces its clauses; enforcement lives in the task ledger, coverage mapping, and evidence directories.
